subject: Invoice schedule alignment & PO lead times for Q4 bookings

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice schedule alignment & PO lead times for Q4 bookings

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to get Acme onboarded for the Q4 deployment. Finance asked me to confirm a couple of timing items so we can determine whether this booking counts in Oct revenue (or rolls to Nov).

Quick ask: can you confirm your internal PO issuance lead time once you receive a final SOW? Typical options we see across customers are 5–15 business days, and that affects whether we can invoice in October. For bookings recognition we usually need: a signed SOW, an issued PO (or vendor commitment), and an invoice to exist within the month. 

I've attached a simple "Invoice-Timing-Matrix" that shows the cutoff windows and the two common paths (PO-before-invoice vs invoice-before-PO with vendor terms). If Acme's procurement can issue a PO by Oct 29, we can route an invoice and have the booking recognized in October. If issuance is later, it will likely push recognition to November.

Options we can pursue now (please indicate preference):
- Option A: Acme issues PO by Oct 29 → Redwood issues invoice by Oct 30 → Oct recognition.
- Option B: Acme approves SOW now, Redwood issues early invoice for 50% up front (requires PO/commitment to finalize) → partial recognition depending on terms.

If you need our vendor legal/company info or a purchase-ready SOW template, I can send both; I included Marissa from Finance and David (CS) on this thread to help with the SOW/PO details.

Attached: Invoice-Timing-Matrix.xlsx (stub)

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Hi Neha —

Appreciate the clarity. Acme procurement typically needs a fully executed SOW + vendor W-9 and 2 business days to validate vendor info, then ~10 business days to route and approve a PO for new vendors. That means if we get SOW and W-9 to procurement by Oct 22, realistic PO issuance is around Nov 5.

Net terms: we operate on Net-30 by default. If Redwood can accept a 50% advance invoice and then final invoice upon PO receipt, I can escalate that to my director (I will flag it as a priority). For large deals we sometimes do split invoicing to meet quarter-based needs.

I am attaching our procurement checklist for new vendors (reference only). Also, please send the SOW and W-9 to procurement@acmedata.com and I'll shepherd it.

Procurement contact: Mark Chen <procurement@acmedata.com>

Thanks —
Susan Park
Director, Partnerships | Acme Data Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice schedule alignment & PO lead times for Q4 bookings

Neha / David —

Thanks for looping Finance in. A couple of important notes from revenue recognition side:

1) Cutoff rules: For us to recognize this as October bookings revenue, we need (a) signed SOW dated in October and (b) either an invoice dated in October with evidence of customer commitment (PO or written procurement confirmation) or an issued PO dated in October. If the PO dates to November, we must move recognition to November.

2) Split invoicing: We can accept a 50% advance invoice now and the balance upon PO issuance — but please flag this as an exception in our internal tracker and confirm approval with Revenue Ops. Splits require a signed revenue exception form for audit.

3) Documentation: Please ensure procurement sends the PO PDF or an approval email chain to revenueops@redwood.com and cc marissa_cole@redwood.com. We prefer a single PDF PO attachment with clear dates.

4) Timing levers: If Acme can provide a conditional commitment email (director-level) confirming intent to issue a PO with a target date, that sometimes suffices alongside an invoice for partial recognition — but it increases audit friction.

I'll attach the booking-recognition-checklist for your reference. Once we have a firm PO target date I'll confirm whether we can close this month.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Finance Manager, Revenue | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: booking-recognition-checklist.pdf (stub)

Hi Susan / Mark —

Thanks for the details and the procurement checklist. Based on Acme's 10-business-day PO routing, it looks like the standard PO timeline would land us in early November and push recognition to November. To keep this in October, here are two pragmatic paths — please indicate which you'd prefer and I'll action immediately:

1) Preferred (fast path): Acme provides a director-level conditional commitment email by Oct 25 and Mark routes the PO to be issued by Oct 29. Redwood will prepare and send an invoice dated Oct 30 upon receipt of the PO. Action items: I will send a purchase-ready SOW and W-9 today; Mark, please confirm you can target Oct 29 PO issuance if we have SOW by EOD Oct 22.

2) Alternate (split invoice): Acme approves SOW now, Redwood issues a 50% advance invoice dated Oct 25. Acme then issues the PO in early Nov and final invoice completes the billing. Note: Finance has asked that we log this as a revenue exception — we will need the signed exception form (Marissa will send).

I linked the HubSpot deal for reference and a DocuSign envelope (SOW) below. If you sign/approve quickly we can escalate internally and prioritize PO routing on your side.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/deal/RINF-7890
DocuSign (SOW): https://docusign.com/REDWOOD/ENV/ABC123

Next steps (proposed):
- Today: I send SOW + W-9 to procurement@acmedata.com (Neha).
- By Oct 25: Acme provides conditional commitment email (Susan).
- By Oct 29: Target PO issued (Mark).
- Oct 30: Redwood issues invoice upon PO submission.

If the timeline slips, please assume recognition defers to November. Thanks everyone — I will follow up with the SOW now.

Cheers,
